 ### 12.4 `governance.json`, `reviews.json` and `discovery.json` — the entry, quality and discovery records
 
 Three further WorkItem-scoped records carry the evidence that the work was *admitted* to the lifecycle on stated grounds, that its artifacts were *judged* rather than merely produced, and — for a brownfield WorkItem — that the repository was *read* before anything was drafted from it.
 
 `governance.json` is written by `governance assess` before `init` and holds the requirements-quality result over the structured check set, the WorkItem classification, the observed risk signals, the deterministic score and level, the hard floors that fired, the final level, the recorded uncertainty, and — for the flow the record proposes — which gates would require a human approval and which would be omittable. Severity, weights, thresholds and floors are read from policy, never from the assessing model's input, and a proposed level below the computed one is recorded as an attempt and has no effect. Run `governance policy` to read the effective values. The lifecycle refuses to advance without a record (`governance_missing`), with a blocking quality failure (`governance_blocked`), or when `requirements/` changed after the assessment (`governance_stale`). `classification.flow` is the one value in the record that the lifecycle consumes: `init` binds it to `state.flow` once, and re-assessing later with a different flow is refused `flow_mismatch` at the next `advance`, `gate approve` or `skip` — ahead of the first ledger append, so a refused command leaves `audit.md` byte-identical.
 
 `reviews.json` is an append-only ledger of artifact reviews: path, content fingerprint at review time, review type, result, actor type and name, evidence id and timestamp. Freshness is **derived** — a review applies to the exact content version it was performed against, and nothing stores a "reviewed" boolean. A gate refuses to approve an artifact with no review (`review_missing`), a review of superseded content (`review_stale`), or a failing review of the current content (`review_failed`); drift re-approval is held to the same rule. Each review is linked into `audit.md` as its own entry, so the ledger answers "who judged this content, and which version" as well as "who approved it."
 
 `discovery.json` is written by `discovery assess` during the `discovery` phase and holds the findings that phase produced: one entry per finding, each with its category, its classification, its statement, the paths it cites and the findings it rests on, plus the per-classification counts and the accepted result. It exists only for a WorkItem whose flow runs `discovery`. The phase has no gate of its own, and the record is what replaces one: `advance` and `skip` both refuse `discovery_missing` until this WorkItem has a record the engine accepted, the record is written before that refusal can be lifted and never partially, and the baseline the completing WorkItem establishes points at it by path and SHA-256 rather than copying it. What the engine guarantees about the classifications, and what remains the author's claim, is set out under the `discovery` phase in §7 — the split is deliberate and `discovery schema` reports both halves.
 
 The recorded gate lists are **evidence of what the assessment implied**, not the thing any decision reads. Every decision re-derives the requirement set from the bound flow, the current record and the policy on disk, so a hand-edited record buys nothing.
 
 **Which gates require a human approval is policy-driven; nothing else about a gate is.** Each gate of the bound flow has one of three dispositions, and they are deliberately distinct facts:
 
 | Disposition | Meaning |
 |---|---|
 | `required` | The bound flow contains this gate and the policy requires a human approval for it. It can be approved or rejected, and nothing else. |
 | `omittable` | The bound flow contains it and the policy does not require an approval. It may still be approved — always permitted, always stricter — or passed by `gate omit`. |
 | `not_in_flow` | The policy names it but the bound flow has no such phase, so the requirement is inert. Reported rather than silently dropped. |

 239: The **persisted active context** is `workitems/.active-context.json`: a
 240: developer-local, gitignored file recording `workitem`, the branch it was set
 241: on, when, and by which command. Only `init` and `workitem use` ever
 242: write it. It is skipped, never fatal, when it is
 243: unreadable, names an unregistered WorkItem, points at a missing directory, or
 244: was set on a different branch - a stale context can never brick a repository,
 245: and `workitem use --clear` restores plain registry-based resolution. It is
 246: deliberately never written by resolution itself, which is what lets the
 247: `PreToolUse` dirty-tree hook run the ladder speculatively without becoming a
 248: second writer.
 249: 
 250: `workitem resolve` runs the same ladder in a reporting posture: it always exits
 251: 0 and returns `resolved`, `rung`, `reason`, the launch directory, the project
 252: root, the current branch and a `candidates` list carrying per-candidate
 253: evidence (`cwd`, `context`, `context:stale`, `branch:<name>`, `runtime`). It is
 254: the only input the orchestrator gets for the ask-the-user rung. The engine
 255: never infers and never returns an inferred answer; the user's choice re-enters
 256: as an explicit `--workitem <id>`.
 257: 
 258: **No rung binds a retired repository-global `.workflow/` runtime**, and none infers one: with zero
 259: WorkItems the ladder answers `none` whether or not legacy state exists, so it never guesses.
 260: `.workflow/` survives as detection only: a project-root marker and the thing a refusal points at.
 261: 
 262: Nothing is stranded by that. `workitem create` is runtime-free, so it never reaches the ladder, and every
 263: other command refuses `workitem_required` with a message that points at it. `init` refuses
 264: `legacy_workflow_present` while a repository-global `.workflow/state.json` exists, regardless of how many
 265: WorkItems are registered, because creating a second runtime beside it would leave two competing records.
 266: SDLE never reads, migrates or writes the retired directory; remove it or move it aside.
 267: 
 268: ### Execution identity
 269: 
 270: Each `init` and each migration stamps `workitems/<id>/.sdle/execution.json`
 271: with an execution id of the form
 272: `<3-letter-git-user-prefix>-<UTC datetime>-<8 hex>`, for example
 273: `muh-20260816T171501Z-1a2b3c4d`. The prefix is `git config user.name`,
 274: lowercased with non-alphanumeric characters removed, truncated to three
 275: characters, falling back to the email local part and finally to `usr`. It is
 276: execution and audit metadata: nothing resolves a WorkItem from it, and it is
 277: never the WorkItem name.
 278: 
 279: The trailing eight hex digits are random. The timestamp has one-second
 280: resolution, and an id is also a key: it names every evidence file
 281: (`governance-<id>.json`, `review-<id>-<n>.json`, `discovery-<id>.json`,
 282: `migration-<id>.json`) and de-duplicates the governance ledger entry. Without
 283: the suffix, two executions in the same second shared both, so the second
 284: overwrote the first one's evidence and never reached the ledger. Each evidence
 285: file is also claimed with an exclusive create before it is written, so an
 286: existing evidence file is never replaced; if no unused id can be found, the
 287: command refuses `execution_id_collision` (exit 3) and records nothing. Ids
 288: written before the suffix existed are read unchanged, because nothing parses
 289: an id. See ADR-009.
 290: 
 291: The same file carries a `git` object - the branch, the starting SHA and the
 292: worktree path the run began on. Missing Git and a detached HEAD are never a
 293: refusal; they simply record `null`. This lives on the execution record rather
 294: than in `state.json` because it describes *this run*, not the workflow, so it
 295: needs no schema version and no migration row.
 296: 
 297: ### Branch and worktree rules
 298: 
 299: One active WorkItem per developer branch or worktree; different WorkItems may
 300: run concurrently; two developers are not expected to drive the same WorkItem in
 301: parallel. There is no distributed locking and no cross-worktree coordination -
 302: the session lock is per-WorkItem, and two `git worktree`s of one repository
 303: each keep their own runtime, their own ledger, their own lock and their own
 304: active context.

-**Applies to:** SDLE v1.17
-
 SDLE **refuses; it does not warn.** A refusal is final, it is structured, and it
 names a way out. Nothing in this document is a workaround: every procedure below
 is the intended path.

 | Code | Meaning | What to do |
 |---|---|---|
 | `0` | Success | — |
 | `1` | **Refused.** A rule said no | Read the reason. Do what it names |
 | `2` | **Usage error.** The invocation was wrong | Fix the flags |
 | `3` | **Integrity failure.** Something on disk is not trustworthy | Stop. Do not "repair" by hand until you have read the section below |
 
 JSON goes to stdout, human text to stderr. Parse the `reason` and `data` fields;
 do not pattern-match the prose.
 
 ---
 
 ## 1. `workitem_required` — nothing is registered

-sdle.sh migrate-workflow --workitem <id>

-
-`migrate-workflow` **never modifies, renames or deletes `.workflow/`.** It is
-left in place, byte for byte, as an archive — whether the migration succeeds,
-refuses, or is interrupted partway through. Re-running an interrupted migration
-is safe.

 repository-wide by nature. Introducing them without a boundary would mean

1: """D06 (SDLE-DEFECT-STABILIZATION-01) - the dry-run transcripts are pinned by
   2: their claims, and every claim is checked against the engine.
   3: 
   4: Transcripts 01-09 used to be byte-pinned against historical commits. A byte
   5: pin says a file did not change; it cannot say the file is *right*, and by this
   6: iteration they were not: Spec Kit paths under `.specify/specs/`, uppercase
   7: fingerprints the engine never prints, no WorkItem or governance step, and a
   8: Gate 7 with no test requirement. The byte pins were released deliberately and
   9: replaced by what this module asserts, for all sixteen transcripts alike:
  10: 
  11: * **structure** - the ten parts the stabilization plan requires (scenario id,
  12:   flow, defect ids, runtime, starting conditions, setup, transcript,
  13:   artifacts/state/audit, negative cases, cleanup, executable coverage) and
  14:   the SIMULATED / PASS-FAIL-BLOCKED-NOT RUN labels;
  15: * **numbers** - every `SDLE_STATE` comment, every status header and every
  16:   `Gate k/T: <label>` prompt is recomputed from the transcript's bound flow
  17:   (`FlowSpec.progress_for`, `gate_number`, `gate_total`, `Constants.label`),
  18:   never from a GREENFIELD habit;
  19: * **refusals** - every `Refused: <reason>` names a reason the engine raises;
  20: * **links** - every test node a transcript cites exists;
  21: * **no regression** - none of the old `.workflow/` literals the T11
  22:   convergence replaced comes back (`DRY_RUN_SUBSTITUTIONS` keeps that list).
  23: 
  24: A transcript that switches WorkItem mid-way (11: brownfield, then iterative)
  25: declares it with an HTML comment, `<!-- dry-run-flow: FLOW -->`, which the
  26: reader never sees and this checker honours from that line on.
  27: """
  28: 
  29: from __future__ import annotations
  30: 
  31: import ast
  32: import re
  33: from pathlib import Path
  34: 
  35: import pytest
  36: 
  37: from conftest import DRY_RUN_SUBSTITUTIONS, REPO_ROOT, sdle
  38: 
  39: DRY_RUNS = REPO_ROOT / "docs" / "dry-runs"
  40: TRANSCRIPTS = sorted(p for p in DRY_RUNS.glob("*.md") if p.name[:2].isdigit())
  41: SCENARIO_COUNT = 16
  42: 
  43: CONSTS = sdle.load_constants(sdle.resolve_paths(
  44:     str(REPO_ROOT), str(REPO_ROOT / ".claude" / "skills" / "sdle")))
  45: 
  46: REQUIRED_ROWS = ("Scenario ID", "Flow", "Purpose", "Defect IDs", "Runtime",
  47:                  "Starting conditions")
  48: REQUIRED_SECTIONS = ("## Setup", "## Transcript",
  49:                      "## Artifacts, state and audit", "## Negative cases",
  50:                      "## Cleanup", "## Executable coverage")
  51: RESULT_LABELS = ("**PASS**", "**FAIL**", "**BLOCKED**", "**NOT RUN**")
  52: 
  53: STATE_COMMENT = re.compile(
  54:     r"<!-- SDLE_STATE phase=(\w+) status=\w+ progress=(\d+)/(\d+) -->")
  55: STATUS_HEADER = re.compile(r"?? SDLE Status: Phase (\d+)/(\d+) - (.+?) \[")
  56: GATE_PROMPT = re.compile(r"Gate (\d+)/(\d+): ([A-Z][A-Za-z ]+? Approval)")
  57: FLOW_SWITCH = re.compile(r"<!-- dry-run-flow: (\w+) -->")
  58: REFUSED = re.compile(r"Refused: `?([a-z_]+)`?")
  59: NODE = re.compile(r"`(tests/[\w/]+\.py)(?:::([\w\[\]\-. ]+))?`")
  60: 
  61: 
  62: def test_there_are_sixteen_transcripts_and_they_are_numbered_densely():
  63:     assert [p.name[:2] for p in TRANSCRIPTS] == [
  64:         f"{n:02d}" for n in range(1, SCENARIO_COUNT + 1)], [
  65:             p.name for p in TRANSCRIPTS]
  66: 
  67: 
  68: def metadata(text: str) -> dict[str, str]:
  69:     rows = {}
  70:     for match in re.finditer(r"^\| \*\*(.+?)\*\* \| (.+?) \|$", text, re.M):
  71:         rows[match.group(1)] = match.group(2)
  72:     return rows
  73: 
  74: 
  75: def bound_flow(text: str) -> str:
  76:     flows = re.findall(r"`([A-Z_]+)`", metadata(text).get("Flow", ""))
  77:     assert flows and flows[0] in CONSTS.flows, flows
  78:     return flows[0]
  79: 
  80: 
  81: @pytest.mark.parametrize("path", TRANSCRIPTS, ids=lambda p: p.name)
  82: def test_every_transcript_carries_the_required_parts(path):
  83:     text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
  84:     rows = metadata(text)
  85:     for row in REQUIRED_ROWS:
  86:         assert row in rows, f"{path.name}: no '{row}' row"
  87:     assert rows["Scenario ID"] == f"DR-{path.name[:2]}", rows["Scenario ID"]
  88:     assert re.fullmatch(r"(-|D0[1-6](, D0[1-6])*)", rows["Defect IDs"]), (
  89:         rows["Defect IDs"])
  90:     for heading in REQUIRED_SECTIONS:
  91:         assert re.search(rf"^{re.escape(heading)}\b", text, re.M), (
  92:             f"{path.name}: missing section {heading!r}")
  93:     assert "**SIMULATED**" in text, path.name
  94:     assert any(label in text for label in RESULT_LABELS), path.name
  95: 
  96: 
  97: def _label_to_phase(flow) -> dict[str, str]:
  98:     return {CONSTS.label(phase, flow): phase for phase in flow.phases}
  99: 
 100: 
 101: @pytest.mark.parametrize("path", TRANSCRIPTS, ids=lambda p: p.name)
 102: def test_every_progress_fraction_and_gate_number_is_the_engines(path):
 103:     """Recomputed from the bound flow, line by line."""
 104:     text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
 105:     flow = CONSTS.flow(bound_flow(text))
 106:     checked = 0
 107:     for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
 108:         switch = FLOW_SWITCH.search(line)
 109:         if switch:
 110:             flow = CONSTS.flow(switch.group(1))
 111:             continue
 112:         where = f"{path.name}:{number}"
 113: 
 114:         for phase, done, total in STATE_COMMENT.findall(line):
 115:             assert phase in flow.phases, (where, phase, flow.name)
 116:             assert f"{done}/{total}" == flow.progress_for(phase), (
 117:                 where, phase, flow.name, flow.progress_for(phase))
 118:             checked += 1
 119: 
 120:         for done, total, label in STATUS_HEADER.findall(line):
 121:             labels = _label_to_phase(flow)
 122:             assert label in labels, (where, label, flow.name)
 123:             assert f"{done}/{total}" == flow.progress_for(labels[label]), (
 124:                 where, label, flow.name, flow.progress_for(labels[label]))
 125:             checked += 1
 126: 
 127:         for number_shown, total, label in GATE_PROMPT.findall(line):
 128:             assert int(total) == flow.gate_total, (where, flow.name)
 129:             expected = f"Gate {number_shown}: {label}"
 130:             gates = {CONSTS.label(phase, flow): phase
 131:                      for phase in flow.gate_phases}
 132:             assert expected in gates, (where, expected, flow.name,
 133:                                        sorted(gates))
 134:             checked += 1
 135:     assert checked, f"{path.name} shows no progress or gate number at all"

 138: def engine_reasons() -> set[str]:
 139:     source = (REPO_ROOT / "scripts" / "sdle.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
 140:     reasons = set(re.findall(
 141:         r'(?:Refused|IntegrityError|UsageError)\(\s*"([a-z_]+)"', source))
 142:     # Some refusals are reported through `emit(..., reason=".")` rather than

 172:     return [(match.group(1), match.group(2)) for match in NODE.finditer(text)]
 173: 
 174: 
 175: @pytest.mark.parametrize("path", sorted(DRY_RUNS.glob("*.md")),
 176:                          ids=lambda p: p.name)
 177: def test_every_cited_test_exists(path):

README.md:47:The block above is the **GREENFIELD** flow — the lifecycle a new project traverses, and the one every pre-flow workflow traversed. A WorkItem may instead be bound to `BROWNFIELD_DISCOVERY`, `ITERATIVE`, `DEFECT_FIX` or `HOTFIX`; each is an ordered subset of the same phase registry, so its `Phase N/M` and `Gate N/M` are that flow's own. The two defect flows additionally run `impact_analysis`, a gateless phase that maps the blast radius of a change before any specification is written; it is still fingerprinted and review-registered like every other governed artifact. `BROWNFIELD_DISCOVERY` additionally runs `discovery`, a gateless phase that reads an existing repository and records a structured set of findings in which every statement carries one of three classifications — observed, inferred or unknown. What the engine checks is that the label is present and is one of those three, that an observation cites a path inside the repository, and that an inference names a basis none of which is itself unknown. What it cannot check is whether the author applied the right label to a given statement; that remains a claim by its author, and saying so is the point. Run `sdle.sh constants` for a flow's exact phase list.

docs/SDLE-Reference-Guide.md:870:The ledger is **tamper-evident**: after every append, the SHA-256 of the entire file is recorded in `state.json → audit_sha`, and verified on every load. A mismatch (edit, truncation, deletion, or a write from another session) halts the workflow until the operator explicitly re-baselines with `accept audit` — an action that is itself logged. Note the precise guarantee: tamper-*evident*, not tamper-*proof* — an actor who edits both `audit.md` and `audit_sha` in `state.json` defeats the check. The defense target is accidental or casual modification, not a determined adversary with full filesystem access. Concurrent-session writes, one common source of accidental corruption, are additionally warned about via the `workitems/<id>/.sdle/lock` session lock.
docs/SDLE-Reference-Guide.md:950:- **The session lock is advisory.** Concurrent sessions are detected and warned about via `workitems/<id>/.sdle/lock`; nothing physically prevents two sessions from writing state simultaneously.

Line 7 also records that the PowerShell forms were not run.","evidence_type":"executed","suggested_fix":"Add a PowerShell-compatible merge and readiness sequence that preserves unrelated settings, then execute it in a disposable target; otherwise explicitly mark the PowerShell path blocked rather than presenting it as complete.","ac_ids":["AC-15","AC-16"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"CX-002","severity":"medium","category":"getting-started-inventory","path":"docs/GETTING-STARTED.md","line":267,"claim":"The promised exact pre-launch inventory is neither exact nor internally consistent. It groups commands, agents, modules, and Spec Kit output into directories instead of listing installed files, while saying every listed path exists even though optional paths and the explicitly absent `workitems/` path are in the same table.","evidence":"Lines 267-283 say `Every path in this table exists`, then list `guidance/` and `.sdle/config.json` as optional and `workitems/` as absent. The table has only `.claude/commands/`, `.claude/agents/sdle-*.md`, and an abbreviated skill directory. Executed `git ls-tree -r` showed 9 command files, 4 agent files, 5 module files, SKILL.md, state.json, 2 hook files, and 3 launch/engine files that should form the exact product inventory.","evidence_type":"executed","suggested_fix":"Publish the complete per-file SDLE inventory with purpose, status, creator, and verification; separately identify dependency-generated variable files and optional or absent paths, and correct the assertion about which paths exist.","ac_ids":["AC-13","AC-15","AC-16"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"CX-003","severity":"medium","category":"reference-correctness","path":"docs/SDLE-Reference-Guide.md","line":43,"claim":"The canonical Reference Guide still describes SDLE as one fixed lifecycle with eight mandatory human gates, contradicting the implemented five-flow, risk-adaptive model.","evidence":"Lines 43 and 45 say `fixed, auditable software delivery lifecycle`, `eight mandatory human approval gates`, and `a fixed sequence`. Executing `python scripts/sdle.py constants` returned five flows with phase counts 18, 19, 16, 14, and 10 and gate totals 8, 8, 7, 6, and 3. The same guide at line 900 states only the final gate is required at every risk level.","evidence_type":"executed","suggested_fix":"Rewrite the executive description around a bound flow selected from the phase registry and risk-derived required gates; describe the 18-phase/eight-gate sequence specifically as GREENFIELD, not the universal product contract.","ac_ids":["AC-03","AC-05"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"CX-004","severity":"medium","category":"removed-contract-documentation","path":"docs/troubleshooting/README.md","line":48,"claim":"Removal of state migration and `migrate-workflow` was not propagated coherently through living documentation. The troubleshooting runbook contains a malformed orphaned migration-refusal table and still directs its explanation through a command that no longer exists; the Reference Guide and ADRs retain additional current-sounding migration claims.","evidence":"Lines 48-56 begin with the orphan delimiter `---|---|`, list `target_exists`, `legacy_state_missing`, `legacy_state_invalid`, and `legacy_audit_broken`, then say `migrate-workflow` would refuse. Executed `rg` found no `cmd_migrate_workflow`, parser registration, `MIGRATIONS`, or `VERSION_MIGRATION` in product code. It did find stale claims at Reference Guide lines 270-282 and in ADR-004, ADR-005, and ADR-008, including an executable-looking `sdle.sh migrate-workflow --workitem <id>` at ADR-008 line 75.","evidence_type":"executed","suggested_fix":"Remove the orphan troubleshooting rows and all current-operational migration claims. Rewrite retained ADR rationale in current terms, preserving history in Git rather than documenting removed handlers, migration evidence, or transition phases as live contracts.","ac_ids":["AC-02","AC-03","AC-05"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"CX-005","severity":"medium","category":"verification-overclaim","path":"docs/README.md","line":33,"claim":"The documentation index overstates dry-run verification by claiming the suite recomputes every claim in the transcripts. The checker validates selected structural and syntactic properties, not all conversational behavior or natural-language assertions.","evidence":"Line 33 says `The test suite recomputes every claim in them from the engine`; dry-runs/README.md similarly says a transcript disagreement fails the build. Inspection of tests/test_dry_run_contracts.py showed checks for required sections, progress/gate numbers, whether displayed refusal identifiers exist somewhere in the engine, cited test-node existence, retired literals, and fingerprint casing. It does not execute or semantically validate every transcript turn, setup, artifact claim, or refusal condition.","evidence_type":"executed","suggested_fix":"Narrow the prose to enumerate exactly the properties recomputed by test_dry_run_contracts.py and keep simulated conversation claims distinct from executed engine evidence.","ac_ids":["AC-07","AC-08","AC-12"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"CX-006","severity":"low","category":"tutorial-drift","path":"docs/tutorials/greenfield-full-tour.md","line":48,"claim":"The full tour still shows `.sdle/templates` in current `config show` output even though DEL-003 removed that member from the engine.","evidence":"The tutorial's JSON at lines 45-50 includes `\"templates\": \".sdle/templates\"`. Current scripts/sdle.py lines 3807-3813 and tests/test_units_repo_config.py lines 450-455 define members as only config, policies, baseline, and implementation_state. Repository-wide search found this as the sole remaining `.sdle/templates` documentation reference.","evidence_type":"executed","suggested_fix":"Remove the templates member from the displayed `config show` response and ensure the tutorial example matches the engine's current JSON exactly.","ac_ids":["AC-06","AC-14"],"confidence":"high"},{"id":"CX-007","severity":"low","category":"directory-layout-documentation","path":"docs/workitems/README.md","line":44,"claim":"The WorkItems guide incorrectly says the session lock is the only ignored path, omitting the developer-local active-context file that the canonical installation now requires users to ignore.","evidence":"Lines 44-46 say `workitems/*/.sdle/lock` is `the only ignored path`. Executed search showed `.gitignore` lines 9-10 and GETTING-STARTED.md line 136 ignore both `workitems/*/.sdle/lock` and `workitems/.active-context.json`; the Reference Guide also calls active-context gitignored and disposable.","evidence_type":"executed","suggested_fix":"List both ignored developer-local paths and reserve the versioned-by-design statement for all other WorkItem content.","ac_ids":["AC-13","AC-15","AC-18"],"confidence":"high"}]}
